newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Rethabile plans JSE debut, more buys.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Rethabile plans JSE debut, more buys.

text.p: Rethabile Group, the South African black empowerment firm which recently bought a stake in Alcatel Altech Telecoms (Pty) Ltd, said on Monday it plans to list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in the next 18 months.

Moss Ngwenya, Rethabile's chief executive officer, said the company, which is also part of a consortium bidding to buy soon-to-be-privatised domestic airline Sun Air SNAJ.CN, was also in talks to buy a stake in another telecommunications firm.
"We are in confidential discussions on acquiring a stake in another telecommunications company," he told Reuters.
"We are looking at listing in the coming 18 months but we want about three or four other portfolio investments in Rethabile before we can list."
It was announced late on Friday that Rethabile Telecoms, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Rethabile, had bought a 20 percent interest in Alcatel Altech Telecoms for 125 million rand.
Alcatel Altech is owned equally by Alcatel CIT of France and South Africa's Allied Technologies Ltd (Altech) ACTJ.J.

Ngwenya said it had not been decided whether Rethabile would debut on the Johannesburg bourse as a whole or whether its telecoms or hotels and leisure unit, its other operating subsidiary, would be the vehicle for the listing.
The initial public offering would be aimed at broadening the firm's shareholder base, targeting especially previously disadvantaged investors, and to raise funds, he said.
"The listing will raise cash to redeem the preference shares held by Alcatel Altech," he said.

In return for each selling a 10 percent stake to Rethabile, Alcatel and Altech will both receive 2.5 million rand in cash and cumulative redeemable participating preference shares in Rethabile Telecoms worth 60 million rand.

Rethabile, in partnership with local airline Comair, has submitted a bid for state-owned airline Sun Air. The consortium is one of four non-binding bids received by the state last month. The names of the shortlisted parties is expected to be announced soon.
